evidence.excerpt: Combining transcriptomic and proteomic measurements can, in principle, improve the accuracy of inferred gene regulatory networks by providing complementary information about regulatory state. We investigated whether joint modelling of RNA-seq and label-free quantitative proteomics data improves Bayesian network structure recovery in salt-stressed soybean, using a dataset of 20 paired samples. Three integration strategies were compared: early integration (concatenated feature matrices), late integration (separately learned networks merged by edge-weight thresholding), and a structured joint BGe scoring approach adapted for heterogeneous measurement types. The joint BGe approach yielded the highest F1 against the reference network (0.49 versus 0.41 and 0.38 for early and late integration, respectively), but required careful normalisation of cross-modality covariance terms. We detail the normalisation pipeline, identify failure modes when proteomics coverage is below 40% of transcriptomic gene set, and propose a practical quality filter for deciding when multi-omics integration is likely to help.
